rows.name: De Haan Relocation

rows.name: Atlas International Movers

rows.name: Windmill Forwarding
rows.description: Overseas moving specialist based in The Hague, serving Amsterdam area. FIDI FAIM-certified. Specialises in groupage moves to 15+ destinations including USA, Australia, South Africa, Thailand, and Caribbean. 17+ years overseas relocation experience.

rows.name: International School of Amsterdam (ISA)

rows.name: Amity International School Amsterdam
rows.description: IB World School in Amstelveen (Amsterdamseweg 204) for ages 3–18. Offers IB Primary Years, Middle Years, and Diploma Programmes. 15 minutes from Schiphol Airport. Inquiry-based curriculum with real-world focus. Part of Amity Education Group.

rows.name: The British School of Amsterdam (BSA)
rows.description: Top-tier British international school for ages 3–18 in Amsterdam, following IB and British National Curriculum. State-of-the-art campus on Havenstraat. Well-regarded for academic results and pastoral care for international families.

rows.name: American School of The Hague (ASH)
rows.description: Accredited American international school in Wassenaar (near The Hague), serving Amsterdam-area expats. Educates students from preschool through Grade 12. 70+ nationalities; 30% American student body. IB and US curriculum. Widely used by corporate expat families.

rows.name: The British School in the Netherlands (BSN)

rows.name: Everaert Advocaten Immigration Lawyers

rows.description: Road-first alternative to air freight: 12+ years, DREAL-licensed, covers western Europe by road and handles the administrative, veterinary and customs formalities, with cabin or hold air options coordinated through CDG, Orly, Beauvais and regional airports. Smaller operator, so capacity, insurance and Norway coverage were all queried in the first pass. SECOND PASS (2026-08-14) answered all three open questions from the operator's own long-distance page. CAPACITY AND CREDENTIALS: confirmed - DDPP Type 2 authorisation, which under Regulation (EC) 1/2005 is the long-journey authorisation for transports over 65 km and over 8 hours, plus the DREAL national and EU licence, ACACED and TAV training, private transport with no groupage, available seven days a week with no weekend, public-holiday or emergency surcharge, quotes inside two hours, and published booking lead times of one week for European road, three to four weeks for air or the UK and four to eight weeks outside the EU. The Nordics appear nowhere in either of its published destination lists (western Europe stops at Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Portugal, Italy and Austria; eastern Europe is quoted case by case), so a Norway origin leg would fall under its 'coordinated with a specialist partner forwarder' clause or its air option, not its own fleet. rows.name: Eurofiscalis
rows.description: Staged for the employer-registration half of the corridor: it publishes guidance for EU employers operating in Norway (NUF, A-melding, D-numbers) and handles cross-border registrations, which is the mirror image of the Norwegian employer's URSSAF firmes-étrangères duty on a NO-FR move. Carried over with the workspace directory's own manual-check flag — depth on personal tax and treaty questions is unconfirmed. SECOND PASS (2026-08-14) answered both halves of the question, and the answer changes what this row is for. THE FRENCH ENTITY IS CONFIRMED, and it is not the shape the first pass assumed: this is a Mougins business (Sophia-Antipolis area, RCS Cannes), not a Paris one, run as three companies at NATURA 1, 1200 avenue du Docteur Maurice Donat — the site publisher (SASU, RCS Cannes 891 611 717), an international VAT compliance and fiscal-representation company (RCS Cannes 834 212 904), and an accountancy company registered with the Ordre des experts-comptables for the PACA region (RCS Cannes 898 006 911) — plus EUROFISCALIS FRANCE (SAS, RCS Cannes 880 371 497), whose corporate object expressly covers acting as fiscal representative of a foreign company for tax and customs declarations. The city field still reads 'national' because it forms part of the import key; correct it to Mougins on the vendor_providers row. THE URSSAF ANSWER IS NO, on the published evidence. Nothing on eurofiscalis.com offers URSSAF service firmes étrangères registration or French payroll for a foreign employer with no French establishment. Its France offer is posted-worker compliance — the SIPSI prior declaration and acting as the mandatory representative in France under the Loi Macron, aimed particularly at transport operators — plus VAT and fiscal representation and an accountancy arm. Those are a DIFFERENT obligation: a posting keeps the employee in the home social-security system on an A1, whereas a Norwegian employer whose employee actually lives and works in France has an employee affiliated to the French regime and must register with URSSAF SFE, obtain a SIRET through the INPI guichet unique, and file DSN (or the free TFE scheme below 20 employees) with prélèvement à la source. RECOMMENDATION: keep Eurofiscalis but re-scope it in customer-facing content to posted-worker compliance, VAT and fiscal representation, and route the URSSAF SFE need to Eurotax (accredited PAS fiscal representative, URSSAF contribution payments, payroll) or RM Boulanger — both staged in vendor_candidates__france_gap_categories_wave2_FR.json for exactly this gap. The personal-tax and treaty depth question is unchanged and remains a professional determination rather than a vendor fact.

rows.name: Orange (France)
rows.contact_phone: 09 69 36 39 00 (dedicated English-language line, Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00; +33 9 69 36 39 00 from abroad, no surcharge)
rows.description: Default telecom recommendation for a newcomer: largest fibre footprint, roughly 500 stores, and the only major operator with an English helpline. Practical corridor detail from the same research: an arriving mover can subscribe with a passport, a temporary French address (hotel accepted) and a SEPA IBAN — a Norwegian account works, so telecom does not have to wait for the French bank account. Conflicting claim to resolve: one Selectra page states Orange's own service 'operates primarily in French', so the English line's scope should be checked before it is promised to a customer. SECOND PASS (2026-08-14) RESOLVED the contradiction: both sources are right about different things. The dedicated English line is real, and confirmed on three independent bases — Orange's own community team publishes the number and its hours, The Connexion's journalists actually rang it and had a person answer in English, and Selectra states Orange is the only major French operator officially providing an English-speaking customer service. The scope is narrow and must be described precisely rather than generously: 09 69 36 39 00, Monday to Friday 09:00–17:00 only, covering technical support and commercial/sales matters, charged at local-call rate and free from an Orange landline, or +33 9 69 36 39 00 from abroad with no surcharge. Everything else at Orange is French — the main 3900 line (Mon–Sat 08:00–20:00) is a French line that may or may not transfer you to an English speaker, the website and online support default to French pages, and in-store English depends on the individual adviser. That is precisely why another source could say Orange's own service 'operates primarily in French' without contradicting the existence of the line. SAFE TO PROMISE A CUSTOMER: a dedicated English line exists, weekday office hours only, and nothing outside them. On pricing: no Livebox figure is recorded on this row and none should be invented — French fibre pricing is promotional and moves monthly, so read it off orange.fr at quote time. The budget anchors in this category are the Bouygues and Free rows.

rows.name: Bouygues Telecom
rows.description: CORRECTED in the second pass (2026-08-14). The first pass recorded Bouygues as the second French operator with a dedicated English-language helpline. That is WRONG and the claim is withdrawn. Selectra's own Bouygues contact page and Echos du Net's contact guide both state plainly that Bouygues does not provide a dedicated English phone line or English chat, that its channels operate primarily in French, and that an individual adviser may help in English only if one happens to be available. So Orange remains the ONLY French major with a dedicated English line, and the first-pass 'both run dedicated English-speaking helplines' phrasing must not be repeated to a customer. What Bouygues is genuinely strong on for this corridor is network and price, not language: ranked no. 1 for WiFi quality in France by ARCEP, fibre up to 8 Gbit/s, a store network for in-person setup where big-city staff are used to international customers, and a no-commitment B&YOU Pure Fibre option. rows.name: Hôpital Franco-Britannique (HFB)
rows.description: Second commonly used English-friendly hospital in the inner western suburbs, staged so the medical category is not single-sourced on the American Hospital. Deliberately thin: only a third-party expat guide was captured — the institution's own site, current group affiliation, address and language provision were not verified in this pass. SECOND PASS (2026-08-14) verified all four from the institution's own site and its foundation, taking the row from T3/0.6 to T1/0.85, and produced a NAME correction. NAME: the institution is now called Hôpital Franco-Britannique (HFB). 'Institut hospitalier franco-britannique' was the name of the 2008 merger of the Hertford British Hospital (founded 1872) and the Hôpital Notre-Dame du Perpétuel Secours (1885); the current name dates from 2019. The name field on this row is left as staged because it forms part of the import key — rename it on the vendor_providers row. OWN SITE: hopitalfrancobritannique.org, which publishes an English section. GROUP AFFILIATION: integrated into the Fondation Cognacq-Jay since 1 January 2021 and presented publicly under Cognacq-Jay Santé; it is an ESPIC, a private non-profit establishment operating inside the French public-service hospital system. ADDRESS: two sites in Levallois-Perret — 4 rue Kléber (main site: adult and paediatric-trauma emergencies 24/7, medicine, surgery, imaging, laboratory, intensive care and the Hartmann radiotherapy centre) and 3 rue Barbès (the former Hertford British Hospital, now the Femme-Mère-Enfant building with a level-2A maternity and 24/7 gynaecological emergencies). Switchboard 01 47 59 59 59, reception open 07:30–20:00 seven days a week; around 275 beds and places, 120 specialists, 17,500 patients and 1,900 births a year. ENGLISH PROVISION: confirmed for general medicine — The Connexion states the hospital offers consultations with an English-speaking doctor at the Levallois site. What it does NOT operate is an international-patient desk of the kind the American Hospital of Paris runs, so English should be confirmed for the specific specialty rather than assumed hospital-wide. THE COMMERCIALLY IMPORTANT FINDING: HFB bills in secteur 1 with no dépassements d'honoraires, so for a CPAM-registered mover it costs nothing beyond the normal co-payment, where the American Hospital is private and expensive. That makes HFB the right DEFAULT English-capable option and the American Hospital the escalation option — the reverse of how the first pass ranked the two.

rows.name: Doctolib (appointment booking with language filters)
rows.description: GUIDANCE CONTENT, NOT A VENDOR — moved out of the vendor shortlist by founder decision on 2026-08-15 (see DECIDED note at the end of this entry). Retained for reference and provenance only. || Platform rather than provider, staged in the medical category as the practical navigation route: search by arrondissement, specialty and language, then verify the practitioner and their sector-1/sector-2 fees on the official Annuaire Santé before booking. Include as a how-to card rather than as a vetted vendor, and keep the emergency instruction alongside it — dial 15 or 112 rather than waiting for an appointment. SECOND-PASS RECOMMENDATION (2026-08-14) for the founder decision: move Doctolib out of the vendor shortlist and into guidance content. The reason is structural, not a judgement on Doctolib. Every field this taxonomy exists to hold is meaningless for a booking platform — there is no accreditation to record, no corridor service to price, no SLA to agree, no contract to sign and nothing a vendor-verification pass could actually verify — so a verified=true flag here would assert something that cannot be true in the sense the other rows mean it. It is also not the only navigation route, and the free official ones are better: the US Embassy in France publishes a list of English-speaking doctors covering Paris, Bordeaux, Lyon, Rennes, Marseille and Strasbourg; the Australian Embassy publishes a comparable list covering Paris, Lille, Lyon, Marseille, Nice/Monaco and Normandy; and the Assurance Maladie's own Annuaire Santé is where a practitioner's registration and sector-1/sector-2 fees can be checked. The honest guidance card is therefore: embassy list or Annuaire Santé first, Doctolib to book, 15 or 112 for an emergency — with the sector-2 warning attached, because English-speaking GPs in Paris and Lyon are disproportionately sector 2, where the state reimburses only the sector-1 base tariff and the excess falls on the patient. If the founder decides platforms DO belong in vendor_providers, the row should stay but the schema needs a provider_type discriminator so a platform is never counted towards a category's provider coverage. Either way nothing breaks: with the wave-2 additions the medical category now holds five genuine providers without this row. DECIDED 2026-08-15 — moved to guidance content, exactly as recommended. Booking platforms do not belong in the vendor shortlist: there is no accreditation to record, no corridor service to price, no SLA to agree and nothing a vendor-verification pass could verify, so a verified flag here could never mean what it means on every other row. This row stays in vendor_providers for provenance but is NOT a vendor — exclude it from vendor shortlists and from the medical category's provider count, and never mark it verified. The guidance itself has been written up as a proper card in docs/france-english-speaking-healthcare-guidance.md, which routes a customer the way this note recommended: embassy English-speaking-doctor list or the Assurance Maladie Annuaire Santé first to find and check a practitioner, Doctolib to actually book, 15 or 112 for an emergency, with the sector-2 fee warning attached. The five genuine providers the medical category now stands on are the American Hospital of Paris, the Hôpital Franco-Britannique, SOS Help, the Hospices Civils de Lyon and Clinique Pasteur Toulouse — so the category still meets the coverage target without this row. The provider_type discriminator floated as a fallback is NOT needed, because that was only required if platforms were kept in the shortlist.

It is often the quickest route for an english speaking GP Paris search, especially if you search by arrondissement, specialty, and consultation type. ... rows.name: AGS Relocation (Paris hub)
rows.description: DO NOT SURFACE — excluded from customer shortlists under the ICP competitor rule, decided 2026-08-15 (see DECIDED note at the end of this entry). Retained for reference and provenance only. || First France-side relocation-management row in the vendor set, and the strongest corridor fit: AGS runs a Paris regional relocation hub AND has its own Norway branch (already staged as a Norway mover), so an FR-NO or NO-FR file can stay inside one group for moving, immigration support, vehicle transfer and pets. Note the workspace ICP rule excludes enterprise RMC competitors (SIRVA, Cartus, CapRelo, Sterling Lexicon, Santa Fe, Crown World Mobility) — AGS Relocation is not on that exclusion list, and founder vetting must still settle the boundary. SECOND PASS (2026-08-14) researched the factual boundary so the decision can be made on evidence, and RECOMMENDS applying the Crown precedent the workspace directory already uses. THE CASE FOR EXCLUSION, in AGS's own words: 'Tailored to meet the specific needs of your business, our assignment management programmes allow you to outsource the administrative and management process', and on its own LinkedIn page 'we support assignees at every step of their relocation and provide support to HR and global mobility teams to ensure compliance and budgetary control'. That is the enterprise-RMC service description almost verbatim, which is what the exclusion list exists to catch. THE CASE AGAINST EXCLUSION: AGS sells to the other end of the market too — 'from large multinational organisations with existing internal mobility programmes, to smaller companies in need of special boutique style relocation assistance' — its own destination-services leadership describes building partnerships with 'corporate from all sectors, relocation management companies', i.e. it supplies RMCs rather than only competing with them, and an independent 2026 market survey categorises AGS as focused on physical move logistics, distinguishing it from the RMC and consulting players. The workspace also already treats AGS as a vendor twice over: AGS Déménagement International and AGS Movers Norway are both verified Moving & Logistics entries in vendor_directory_by_city_frno.md. RECOMMENDATION: split the group exactly as that directory already splits Crown, where 'the Crown Relocations moving brand remains OK' while Crown World Mobility is excluded — treat AGS's moving and destination-services brands as vendors, and treat the 'AGS Relocation' assignment-management programme as the competitor-adjacent product that is never surfaced. If the founder prefers a clean exclusion instead, the rmc category no longer depends on this row: Management Mobility Consulting, Home Conseil Relocation, Easy Lyon and See & Moove are all staged in vendor_candidates__france_gap_categories_wave2_FR.json, all SME-scale, and three of the four carry a EuRA or ReloQI quality seal. DECIDED 2026-08-15 — the Crown precedent is APPLIED, exactly as recommended. AGS's moving and destination-services brands remain eligible vendors: that is the ten 'AGS Movers' rows already carried in vendor_providers (Paris, Oslo, Munich, Frankfurt, Barcelona, Madrid, Rotterdam, Dublin, Manchester, Geneva), all of which stay available. The 'AGS Relocation' assignment-management programme is treated as competitor-adjacent and is NEVER surfaced to a customer. THIS ROW IS THAT PROGRAMME, so it is now do-not-surface: exclude it from every customer shortlist, quote and recommendation, do not count it towards the rmc category's provider coverage, and never flip it to verified. Nothing is lost on the corridor itself — the single-group door-to-door benefit this row was originally staged for still holds through AGS's Paris moving arm (AGS France / AGS Movers Paris) and its Oslo arm (AGS Movers Norway), which sit in the mover_international category and are unaffected. The surfaceable rmc shortlist is Grospiron, Management Mobility Consulting, Home Conseil Relocation, Easy Lyon and See & Moove — five, so the category still meets the coverage target without this row. ONE ROW OUTSIDE THIS SCOPE catches the same rule: 'AGS Relocation Munich' (external_id prov-rmc-de-munich-ags-relocation-munich) is the only other AGS entry sitting in the rmc category. It belongs to a different corridor's data set and has deliberately NOT been touched here — flagged so the same precedent can be applied to it.

rows.description: Fifth pet row, staged deliberately as the local handover leg rather than as an international shipper. Its stated authorisation is DDPP Type 1, which under Regulation (EC) 1/2005 covers journeys up to 8 hours — Type 2 is the long-journey authorisation, as Cathy Pets' own site confirms for journeys over 65 km and over 8 hours. So the honest use for this operator is the door-to-CDG/Orly freight-zone transfer and the 24/7 emergency pet taxi around Paris, feeding one of the air operators already staged, not the Oslo–Paris sector itself. rows.name: Henner
rows.description: Fifth insurance row and the second insurer on the CFE's own partner list that also sells a first-euro contract — which matters, because the CFE route is only open to people carrying French social-security rights abroad, so a Norwegian-national mover arriving in France needs the first-euro product, not the top-up. Henner runs its own medical network (stated as 68,000 practitioners across 19-plus countries) and has both an individual and a collective/corporate arm, so the same provider can serve an employer scheme and a self-funded mover. Management address 14 boulevard du Général Leclerc, CS 20058, 92527 Neuilly-sur-Seine Cedex. Two facts worth carrying into corridor content: cover cannot be taken out for residence in the United States, the UAE, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria or Crimea (Norway and France are unaffected), and joining the CFE more than 3 months after leaving France triggers a CFE waiting period during which nothing is reimbursed — a real FR-NO timing trap. Note this is a taxonomy addition, not a new company: Henner already exists in vendor_providers under healthcare_navigation. Its ORIAS registration number was not captured in this pass.

Avec Henner Expat Santé, vous avez le choix d'une assurance santé qui intervient dès le 1er euro dépensé ou en complément de la Caisse des français de l'Etranger. ... Accident au 1er euro (uniquement pour le complément CFE) : si vous souscrivez plus de 3 mois après votre départ de France auprès de la CFE, un délai de carence vous sera appliqué. rows.name: Eurotax
rows.description: This is the row the legal_admin category was actually missing. When a Norwegian employer with no French establishment has an employee living and working in France, the employee falls under the French social-security regime and the employer must register with the URSSAF service firmes étrangères, obtain a SIRET via the INPI guichet unique, file monthly (DSN, or the free TFE scheme below 20 employees) and operate prélèvement à la source. Eurotax is accredited by the French tax administration as a fiscal representative and covers exactly that chain: PAS representation, URSSAF contribution payments and, on its top tier, paying the salaries. Corridor-specific detail from its own FAQ: because Norway is EEA, the employer may operate PAS itself only if it holds a SEPA B2B account the French tax administration can debit, and Eurotax conditions the EEA route on two bilateral conventions with France (administrative assistance against fraud, and mutual assistance in tax recovery) — whether both are in force for Norway is a professional determination, not a vendor question. Three published service tiers (Basique, Standard, Package complet) with no published prices; site in FR/EN/DE/IT/ES. Head-office address not captured: its own locations page renders from a script.

attributes.source_name: Eurotax own site (French withholding-tax and payroll services page, including its own PAS obligations FAQ)
attributes.evidence_quote: Eurotax fournit des services de la gestion du prélèvement à la source, des contributions sociales et le paiement des salaires pour les entreprises non françaises ayant des salariés en France. ... Eurotax est agréé par l'administration fiscale française en tant que représentant fiscal des sociétés établies hors de France. ... Eurotax vous aide dans vos versements de cotisations sociales auprès des différents organismes (URSSAF – Assurance…) ... Si votre entreprise est établie dans l'UE ou dans un État de l'Espace économique européen (EEE), vous devez disposer d'un compte SEPA B2B qui permettra à l'administration fiscale française (AFF) d'effectuer des prélèvements. Si vous n'avez pas de compte SEPA B2B, la désignation d'un représentant fiscal devient obligatoire afin de gérer la retenue à la source.
attributes.accreditation_body: Accredited fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) certified by the French tax administration

rows.name: RM Boulanger
rows.description: The second France-side employer-compliance option, and the one that fits when the Norwegian employer is POSTING someone rather than relocating them. The corridor must not conflate the two obligations: a genuine posting keeps the employee in the Norwegian scheme on an A1 certificate and triggers a SIPSI prior declaration plus a designated representative in France, whereas a real relocation makes the employee French-affiliated and triggers URSSAF service firmes étrangères registration and French payroll. RMB covers the posting side (SIPSI filing, acting as the French representative, handling labour-inspection enquiries, BTP cards for construction work) plus withholding-tax compliance and payroll administration for foreign companies, through a client platform it calls Post & Work. It offers a free first check-up, which is a low-friction way to establish which of the two regimes a given NO-FR case is actually in. Site in EN/FR. Its published number is a Nord (03 20) line; the head-office address was not captured in this pass.

RMB supports you with your obligations concerning the posting of workers: Preparation and submission of your SIPSI declarations, Acting as the representative for your posted workers, Handling enquiries from the French labour authorities ... RMB assists clients that have employees working in France in order to be compliant. RM Boulanger supports foreign companies with their payroll administration.

rows.name: Welcoming Agency
rows.description: International-mobility relocation agency with offices in Madrid and Barcelona. Home search, real-estate personal shopper, school/education advisory and temporary stays; serves both individuals and corporate teams. 5.0 Google rating (300+ families supported).

rows.name: MovingToSpain (Rental Search)
rows.description: English-speaking long-term rental search service operating across Spain including Madrid. Assists newcomers with property search, viewings and lease negotiation.

rows.name: Engel & Völkers Madrid
rows.description: International premium real-estate brand with market centres across Madrid. Serves expat buyers and tenants seeking high-end residential rentals and purchases; multilingual English-language service.

rows.name: Idealista (Property Portal)
rows.description: Spain's leading online property portal, widely used by expats to search Madrid rentals and purchases. English-language interface; connects users with hundreds of local agencies.

rows.name: Lexmovea
rows.description: Madrid immigration law firm handling NIE and TIE, residence permits (Digital Nomad, non-lucrative, EU family, arraigos), visas, Beckham Law and relocation/settling-in support for foreign nationals. WhatsApp +34 611 44 42 01.

rows.name: Winkels Abogados
rows.description: Madrid law firm with 25+ years in immigration law: NIE, residence/work authorisations, EU-citizen residence certificates, Golden Visa, highly-qualified and intra-company transfer permits, arraigos, renewals and nationality. Handles police-station appointments for fingerprinting and card collection.

rows.name: Abogacía Extranjería
rows.description: Madrid immigration law firm covering residence and work permit applications, appeals, and deportation defence for foreign nationals. Secondary phone +34 649 117 806.

rows.name: TG Legal Consulting
rows.description: Immigration law practice assisting foreign nationals with regularisation, residence and work permits, and related administrative procedures in Spain.

rows.name: MySpainVisa
rows.description: Team of Spanish immigration lawyers handling NIE numbers, TIE residence cards, complex residency applications and corporate relocations; serves clients relocating to Madrid.

rows.name: Cigna Global (Cigna Healthcare)
rows.description: Global IPMI carrier offering modular international health plans (core hospitalization plus optional outpatient, maternity, dental, medical evacuation) with cover in 200+ countries. Popular for internationally mobile employees who need continuity of cover across borders during and after relocation. Explicit country coverage pages for Spain and other EU markets.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Strong choice for cross-border continuity — cover moves with the employee rather than resetting per country. IPMI is an informational vendor category; ReloPass introduces the provider, it does not give insurance advice. Confirm whether local statutory cover (e.g. Norway's folketrygden, Ireland/Spain public schemes) is also required alongside IPMI.
attributes.pricing_model: Annual premium per insured; modular (choose coverage area, benefit level, add-ons); tiered by age and region
attributes.price_range_eur: Indicative individual comprehensive plans ~€1,800–€6,000/yr; quotes are individualized by age, area of cover and modules

rows.name: Allianz Care
rows.description: International health insurance arm of Allianz (operations based in Dublin, Ireland), providing individual and group IPMI plans with worldwide cover, Expat Assistance programme and A+ (A.M. Best) rating. Well suited to group/employer schemes for relocating staff across European corridors.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Dublin-based operation makes it a natural fit for ES-IE (Dublin) group cover. Offers employer group schemes — relevant when an SME wants one policy across multiple moves. Informational vendor only; ReloPass does not advise on insurance selection.
attributes.pricing_model: Annual premium per insured; individual and group (employer) schemes; benefit and region tiers with optional modules
attributes.price_range_eur: Indicative individual plans ~€1,700–€6,500/yr; group/employer pricing negotiated by headcount; quotes individualized

rows.name: Bupa Global
rows.description: International division of Bupa offering premium IPMI for individuals, families and companies, with worldwide and region-specific cover and a large direct-billing hospital network. Positioned at the higher-service end of the expat market.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Premium end of the market with strong direct-billing network — good where the employee wants minimal out-of-pocket friction. Higher premiums than mid-market carriers. Informational vendor only.
attributes.pricing_model: Annual premium per insured; individual, family and corporate plans; area-of-cover and benefit tiers
attributes.price_range_eur: Indicative individual comprehensive plans ~€2,500–€8,000/yr (premium tier); quotes individualized by age/area/modules

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: US-based international car shipping company (40+ years) offering container and RoRo vehicle transport to Finland with customs clearance and door-to-door delivery.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Non-EU-origin vehicles into Finland trigger customs duty + VAT plus Finnish car tax (autovero, declared to vero.fi). Removal-goods tax relief may apply via Finnish Customs (tulli.fi) if residence/ownership conditions are met. Vehicle must pass Finnish roadworthiness inspection and meet EU/Finnish emissions standards before registration.

rows.name: West Coast Shipping
rows.description: International car shipping specialist (17+ years) moving vehicles between the US and Europe including Finland, offering container consolidation, insurance and customs coordination.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Finnish car tax (autovero) is model-specific and often the largest single cost item; budget it separately from freight. EU-origin used vehicles avoid customs duty but still face autovero and registration inspection.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: International auto shipping to France via major ports (Le Havre, and onward to Paris/Lyon) with container and RoRo options and full customs paperwork handling.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Non-EU-origin cars into France face ~6.5-10% EU customs duty plus 20% TVA (VAT). A quitus fiscal (tax clearance) and homologation / reception a titre isole (individual type approval) are required before registration (carte grise). VAT relief possible under transfer-of-residence rules if owned 6+ months.

rows.name: West Coast Shipping
rows.description: US-to-Europe car shipping specialist handling pickup, US export clearance and French customs coordination with delivery to France.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Homologation is the common bottleneck: US-spec vehicles may require modifications and a certificate of conformity (COC) or DREAL individual approval before a carte grise can be issued. Factor homologation lead time into the move timeline.

rows.name: A1 Auto Transport
rows.description: International vehicle shipping company with a broad carrier network moving cars to French ports including Bordeaux, handling documentation and customs.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Required documents typically include the vehicle title, registration, photo ID, shipping authorization and customs forms. Confirm the vehicle title is clear of liens before export.

rows.name: Autoshippers Car Shipping
rows.description: UK-based international car shipping company moving vehicles by container and RoRo worldwide, with import and export handling to/from the UK.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Importing a car to the UK requires a NOVA (Notification of Vehicle Arrival) to HMRC within 14 days, payment of import VAT (20%) and duty (10% on cars from outside the UK), IVA/type approval, then DVLA registration. Transfer-of-Residence (ToR) relief can waive VAT/duty for returning residents who owned the car 6+ months.

rows.name: CARS Worldwide
rows.description: Worldwide car transportation, storage and customs clearance provider with offices across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Handles customs clearance in-house across multiple regions, useful for multi-leg corporate moves. Confirm whether the UK IVA test and DVLA registration are included or handled by the employee.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: International car shipping to the UK from the US with offices in both countries, managing the import process, container/RoRo transport and customs.

attributes.notes_for_hr: US-spec cars usually require an IVA (Individual Vehicle Approval) test before DVLA registration. Budget for the NOVA/HMRC step within 14 days of arrival to avoid penalties.

rows.name: A1 Auto Transport
rows.description: International vehicle shipping to Luxembourg (typically routed via Antwerp) with insured door-to-door service and customs documentation support.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Luxembourg has no seaport; vehicles usually arrive via Antwerp (Belgium) and are trucked in. Registration is handled by the SNCA (snca.lu). Used cars imported as removal goods may be VAT-exempt if owned 6+ months with 6000+ km; see guichet.public.lu.

rows.name: SDC International Shipping
rows.description: International moving and vehicle shipping company handling relocations to Luxembourg via Antwerp, including household goods and car import/customs.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Can bundle car import with a household-goods container. Confirm duty-free customs eligibility under transfer-of-residence and SNCA registration steps up front.

rows.name: Ship Overseas
rows.description: International car shipping company transporting vehicles from US ports to Qatar's Hamad Port with customs and documentation support.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Vehicles enter via Hamad Port. Qatar applies ~5% customs duty on the CIF value; cars must generally be GCC-spec / left-hand-drive and have valid documentation. Residency/registration steps require Qatari ID (QID).

rows.name: Santa Fe Relocation
rows.description: Global relocation firm with local Middle East offices offering car shipping and full destination services including customs clearance and registration support in Qatar.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Enterprise-grade relocation provider that can manage the full door-to-door move plus car import as one engagement. On-the-ground office helps with Qatari registration formalities.

rows.name: West Coast Shipping
rows.description: International car shipping company that has historically published guidance and routes for shipping vehicles from the US to Russia (Moscow / St Petersburg).

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION / LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED: post-2022 sanctions severely restrict logistics and vehicle shipments to Russia; many carriers have suspended service and payment channels are constrained. Russian import duties on cars are very high (commonly 5000-15000+ EUR equivalent). Confirm current sanctions compliance and carrier availability before quoting or committing.

rows.name: SDC International Shipping
rows.description: International moving company publishing relocation and vehicle-import guidance for moves from the US to Russia.

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION / LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED: sanctions and service suspensions make Russia car import highly uncertain in 2026. Import duties depend on model, year and engine volume and are among the highest globally. Treat any quote as provisional pending a live sanctions and carrier check.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: International car shipping to Saudi Arabia (Dammam, Jeddah) with 40+ years experience, container/RoRo transport and customs paperwork handling.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Saudi Arabia restricts used-car imports: vehicles must generally be 5 model-years old or newer, left-hand-drive, and meet SASO conformity standards. ~5% customs duty on CIF value. Certain models and salvage/flood titles are barred.

rows.name: Santa Fe Relocation
rows.description: Global relocation provider offering car shipping and destination services into Saudi Arabia with local offices handling customs and registration.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Full-service option for corporate moves; local team assists with SASO conformity and Absher/Muroor registration. Confirm the 5-year vehicle age limit and LHD requirement before shipping.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: International shipping company handling relocations and vehicle transport to Thailand with customs clearance and door-to-door delivery.

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION: Thailand imposes some of the world's highest car import duties (combined taxes can reach ~200-328% of value). Used-vehicle import is largely restricted to returning residents / work-permit holders meeting strict ownership criteria. Buying locally is almost always cheaper than importing.

rows.name: Santa Fe Relocation
rows.description: Global relocation firm with Thailand offices offering car shipping and destination services including customs handling and registration support.

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION: Thai import taxes on cars are extremely high and eligibility is tightly restricted. Have the local team confirm import permit eligibility (import license from the Department of Foreign Trade) before committing to a move that assumes the employee keeps their car.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: International car shipping to Turkey moving hundreds of cars monthly via container and RoRo with customs documentation support.

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION: Turkey generally prohibits permanent import of used foreign-registered vehicles by individuals. Returning Turkish citizens resident abroad 185+ days may import under the 'accompanied vehicles' regime (ticaret.gov.tr). Foreign expats typically only get temporary import. Confirm eligibility before shipping.

rows.name: ODS Orient
rows.description: Freight forwarder specialising in RoRo car shipping to Turkey, handling B/L, commercial invoice and Turkish customs requirements.

attributes.notes_for_hr: RoRo transit to Turkey is typically 7-12 days. Turkish customs require the original bill of lading, commercial invoice and vehicle documents. Same import-eligibility caution applies (permanent import restricted for non-citizens).

rows.name: West Coast Shipping
rows.description: International car shipping specialist handling vehicle collection, condition reporting, US export clearance and secure transport to Turkey.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Freight to Turkey commonly runs ~3900-5400 EUR equivalent before duties. Verify the employee's import eligibility (citizen-returning vs temporary) before booking, as Turkish rules can make permanent import impossible for foreign nationals.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: International car shipping to Ukraine (historically via Odesa port) with customs clearance and onward delivery.

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION / SECURITY REVIEW: active conflict conditions disrupt Ukraine's Odesa port and sea routes; some shipments route overland via Poland instead. Ukrainian import charges include excise, VAT and duty. Verify current port operability, insurance coverage and security before committing.

rows.name: Seaway Export
rows.description: Vehicle, boat and heavy-equipment shipping company offering door-to-border transport to Ukraine with customs clearance.

attributes.notes_for_hr: HR CAUTION / SECURITY REVIEW: advertises door-to-border service with 25-35 day transit; wartime conditions can change routing and timelines. Confirm live security and insurance terms before relying on any timeline.

rows.name: Schumacher Cargo Logistics
rows.description: US-based international car shipping company (40+ years) importing and exporting vehicles worldwide via container and RoRo with full customs handling.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Importing a car into the US requires EPA (emissions) and DOT/NHTSA (safety) conformity; non-conforming vehicles must go through a Registered Importer (RI) and Independent Commercial Importer (ICI). CBP entry (form 7501), ~2.5% duty on passenger cars (25% on trucks). Vehicles 25+ years old are exempt from EPA/DOT conformity.

rows.name: A1 Auto Transport
rows.description: Vehicle shipping company with a broad carrier network offering domestic and international car, boat and equipment transport to and from the US.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Handles both import into the US and export out. For inbound moves, confirm EPA/DOT conformity path (direct-import 25-year exemption vs RI/ICI) before shipping a foreign-spec vehicle.

rows.name: West Coast Shipping
rows.description: International car shipping specialist (17+ years) moving vehicles between the US and EU, UK, Middle East and Australia with instant-quote and door-to-door service.

attributes.notes_for_hr: Strong on US-EU/UK lanes with container consolidation to reduce cost. For US inbound, verify emissions/safety conformity requirements early to avoid the vehicle being held or refused at the port.

rows.description: IATA- and IPATA-certified pet air transport specialist (IPATA member #517, member since 2010) with offices in Barcelona and Madrid, handling international door-to-door pet shipping including documentation, IATA-compliant crates and customs. caveats: Registered office and IPATA primary airport are Barcelona (BCN); Madrid is a second office and MAD is a served (secondary) airport. The row stays filed under Madrid because it is being used for the ES->IE-out-of-Madrid corridor.

No Ireland-specific customer references were found. Corridor capability is established from accreditation, in-house customs/freight/vet services and the carrier panel rather than from a documented ES->IE case.

accreditation.notes: IPATA profile 517 resolves to Baggage Pets (A Division of Sistemes Internacionals de Carrega s.l.). Registry shows Active Member - Regular, not dropped, dues paid through 2027, joined 2010, association id_number 337.
